history.dynasty: Not applicable - a natural rock formation
history.period: Discovered July 2004 (claimed 1,000 years old by one listing - unverified)
history.summary: Shiva temple at Sivey/Old Ziro in the Kardo forest, home to what is described as the world's largest natural Shiva linga - about 25 feet tall and 22 feet in circumference, at 5,754 ft altitude in the Apatani plateau, discovered in July 2004 by woodcutter Prem Subha when a felled tree exposed it. Natural rock forms beside it are revered as Parvati and Ganesha (with a manmade Nandi installed in 2016), and water flows continuously from the linga's base. Local priests cite a Shiva Purana (Rudra Khanda) prophecy of Shiva's fiery form manifesting at 'Lingalaya', later called Arunachal. Conflict: one listing claims the site is 1,000 years old and ASI-managed, while detailed accounts describe no built temple, only a well, havan kund and bells, with priests present dawn to dusk. Coordinates decoded from the temple's Google Plus Code (7MVMHQ4P+FPJ, sivey, Old Ziro) - approximate (verify).

name: Shree Siddheshwar Nath Temple
town_description: Ziro is a plateau town in Lower Subansiri district, heartland of the Apatani tribe famed for its wet-rice cultivation, pine hills and bamboo groves. One of Arunachal's oldest towns and a UNESCO World Heritage tentative site, it hosts the annual Ziro Festival of Music and is a base for exploring Talley Valley and nearby temples.

travel.airport: Donyi Polo Airport (Hollongi/Itanagar), about 100 km away (4-hr drive); Lilabari (Assam) about 123 km
travel.railway: Naharlagun railway station, about 100 km away (3-hr shared taxi)
travel.road: NH-13 (Trans-Arunachal Highway); Ziro is about 115 km from Itanagar and 450 km from Guwahati; the temple is about 4 km from Hapoli township, reached by a treacherous forest path

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (dry season); Maha Shivratri draws the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Dawn to dusk (priests on site); devotees throng on Mondays, Sundays and during Shravan
